title: Ledger and Compass
premise: In the winter of 1799, Elodie Sandoval, a discreet courier for a collapsing republic, is stranded in the mountain town of Val-Brume when the season's last bridge closes behind her. Carrying a coded ledger that could indict the republic's own heroes — or its conquerors — she must decide whether to deliver it, destroy it, or make it speak. Sheltered by a widowed ferryman's family and hunted by both loyalist agents and the republicans who sent her, she discovers the ledger's true author was her own presumed-dead mother. In the end, Elodie chooses justice over obedience: she copies the ledger, hides the original, and delivers the truth into the hands of a printer and a judge on the century's final night, buying the record a life beyond any regime.
about_author: Marguerite Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seized diplomatic papers in provincial European collections. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Elodie, posing as a wool merchant's clerk, crosses into Val-Brume hours before the bridge chains go up for winter. POV: Elodie. Beat: quiet competence shadowed by the dread of being cut off from her route.

chapters.title: A Room Above the Cooperage
chapters.summary: She takes lodgings with the ferryman Aurel Vasse and his sharp-eyed daughter Sabine, hiding the ledger in a false bottom of her trunk. POV: Elodie. Beat: the strain of constant performance.

chapters.title: Instructions in Cipher
chapters.summary: A dead-drop letter orders her to wait for a contact named 'the Notary' who never arrives. POV: Elodie. Beat: first crack of doubt about who still commands her.

chapters.title: The Town That Counts Everything
chapters.summary: Val-Brume's notary, Maître Corbineau, keeps obsessive civic records; Elodie realizes the town itself is a ledger of the republic's crimes and kindnesses. POV: Elodie. Beat: fascination, the archivist's itch.

chapters.title: Sabine's Map of the Ice
chapters.summary: Sabine teaches Elodie the frozen river paths, and an unlikely friendship forms over shared contempt for being underestimated. POV: Elodie. Beat: warmth, first loyalty outside duty.

chapters.title: A Man Who Claims the Road
chapters.summary: Loyalist agent Duvall arrives claiming authority over all winter traffic, and Elodie recognizes his seal from the ledger's margin. POV: Elodie. Beat: cold fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Working by candlelight, Elodie deciphers the first pages: requisitions, executions, and payments signed by men now celebrated as liberators. POV: Elodie. Beat: vertigo — her own side is implicated.

chapters.title: The Notary's Request
chapters.summary: Corbineau, suspecting what she carries, asks her not to bring 'another fire' into his town; his own brother vanished in a purge. POV: Elodie. Beat: guilt and the pull of a witness's duty.

chapters.title: Aurel's Ferry, Burned
chapters.summary: Aurel's ferry is torched by men hunting an earlier courier; the family shelters Elodie anyway. POV: Elodie. Beat: debt of gratitude hardening into obligation.

chapters.title: The Second Courier
chapters.summary: A wounded stranger, Tomas, arrives over the ice carrying a duplicate key to Elodie's cipher — and dies before explaining. POV: alternating Elodie and Sabine. Beat: grief and the sense of a net closing.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Courtesy
chapters.summary: Duvall hosts a polite dinner, probing every guest; Elodie survives by lying fluently and hating how good she has become at it. POV: Elodie. Beat: self-alienation.

chapters.title: Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie recognizes her dead mother's handwriting in the ledger's annotations — the woman who taught her codes did not die in the purge; she wrote the indictment. POV: Elodie. Beat: shattered grief turning to fierce inheritance.

chapters.title: The Convent Archive
chapters.summary: Following her mother's marginal marks, Elodie and Sabine search a suppressed convent's papers and find a hidden correspondence. POV: Elodie. Beat: awe, the thrill of the hunt.

chapters.title: Corbineau's Confession
chapters.summary: The notary admits he certified one of the purge's false inventories to save his own family. POV: Corbineau. Beat: shame, and the theme of complicity made personal.

chapters.title: Duvall Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Duvall, knowing more than he lets on, offers Elodie passage out in exchange for the ledger 'for safekeeping.' POV: Elodie. Beat: temptation — the easy exit versus the hard truth.

chapters.title: Sabine Follows the Smoke
chapters.summary: Sabine secretly trails Duvall's men to a cache of seized documents meant for burning. POV: Sabine. Beat: courage, and the cost of knowing too much.

chapters.title: The Burning at the Mill
chapters.summary: Elodie witnesses papers burn and saves a single scorched page — proof the destruction is deliberate, ordered from above. POV: Elodie. Beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: A Republic of Two
chapters.summary: Elodie and Sabine swear a private pact: the record will survive even if they don't. POV: Elodie. Beat: loyalty redefined — not to a state, but to truth.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Drop
chapters.summary: Elodie tests the old dead-drop and walks into Duvall's ambush, escaping only because Corbineau vouches for her. POV: Elodie. Beat: terror, and a debt to a compromised man.

chapters.title: Winter Deepens
chapters.summary: A blizzard seals the town; food runs short and neighbors turn on each other, a small rehearsal of the nation's collapse. POV: Sabine. Beat: claustrophobia and moral erosion.

chapters.title: The Judge Who Wintered Here
chapters.summary: A retired judge, Madame Liorans, winters in Val-Brume; Elodie risks showing her one deciphered page. POV: Elodie. Beat: hope with a blade in it — justice may have an address after all.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Elodie rereads her orders and realizes her handlers intended the courier to die with the ledger, erasing the evidence. POV: Elodie. Beat: betrayal; the old loyalty dies.

chapters.title: The Copyist's Discipline
chapters.summary: Elodie begins copying the ledger in duplicate, hiding pages in the cooperage's barrel staves. POV: Elodie. Beat: patient, monastic determination.

chapters.title: Duvall Closes In
chapters.summary: A search of the town's lodgings forces Elodie to move the original into the frozen crypt beneath the convent. POV: Elodie. Beat: near-catastrophe, nerves fraying.

chapters.title: Aurel's Price
chapters.summary: Aurel is arrested on old smuggling charges as leverage; the town must choose between silence and solidarity. POV: Aurel. Beat: an ordinary man's dignity under pressure.

chapters.title: The Town Signs Its Name
chapters.summary: Corbineau, redeeming himself, opens the civic registers and deposes witnesses — Val-Brume puts its own testimony on the record. POV: Corbineau. Beat: collective courage.

chapters.title: The Notary's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corbineau's records corroborate the cipher page by page; Elodie weaves the two into a single indictment. POV: Elodie. Beat: the joy of the record becoming undeniable.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Cooperage
chapters.summary: A lodger sells Elodie out; Duvall raids the cooperage and finds the staves empty, but takes Sabine hostage. POV: Elodie. Beat: despair and guilt — her cause now costs others.

chapters.title: The Exchange on the Ice
chapters.summary: Elodie offers herself for Sabine at the frozen crossing; Duvall accepts, planning to bury courier and ledger together. POV: Sabine. Beat: sacrifice, and the terror of being worth it.

chapters.title: Madame Liorans Intervenes
chapters.summary: The judge invokes archaic writ and demands Duvall show lawful authority before any prisoner leaves his jurisdiction. POV: Liorans. Beat: the law as a thin but real shield.

chapters.title: The Hearing in the Salt House
chapters.summary: An improvised hearing: Duvall's forged commissions unravel under Corbineau's registry evidence. POV: Elodie. Beat: the intoxication of truth prevailing in a room.

chapters.title: Duvall's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Escaping judgment, Duvall seizes the convent crypt and the original ledger, and sends for soldiers coming with the thaw. POV: Elodie. Beat: everything gained now at risk.

chapters.title: The Century's Last Week
chapters.summary: The town races the calendar: copies must reach a printer in the valley before the year — and the victors' historians — turn. POV: Elodie. Beat: urgency, purpose, no more hiding.

chapters.title: Sabine's Route
chapters.summary: Sabine guides the copies down the dangerous river ice with the duplicate set, while Elodie stays as decoy. POV: Sabine. Beat: the student becomes the courier.

chapters.title: The Fire in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Duvall burns the convent above the crypt to destroy the original; Elodie, hiding inside, barely survives the collapse. POV: Elodie. Beat: the cost of originals — and why copies matter.

chapters.title: What Survives the Fire
chapters.summary: The scorched page and Corbineau's registers remain; Elodie realizes the town's testimony is now the strongest evidence. POV: Elodie. Beat: grief transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: The Reckoning at the Bridge
chapters.summary: As the thaw opens the crossing, Elodie confronts Duvall before the assembled town and the arriving soldiers, reading the indictment aloud. POV: Elodie. Beat: the climax — voice against violence.

chapters.title: The Arrest of Agent Duvall
chapters.summary: Madame Liorans, with Corbineau's registers and the soldiers' own orders, takes Duvall into lawful custody — justice inside the law at last. POV: Liorans. Beat: catharsis, order restored but changed.

chapters.title: New Year's Print Run
chapters.summary: News arrives that the copies reached the printer; the indictment is set in type on the century's final day. POV: Elodie. Beat: quiet triumph — the record outlives them all.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Compass
chapters.summary: Elodie, freed from her orders, chooses to stay through spring as the town's archivist, her mother's ledger deposited with the judge, and a new compass point: witness, not courier. POV: Elodie. Beat: resolution — inheritance claimed, truth on the record, a life of her own begun.
